prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A nuclear magnetic resonance flowmeter comprising at least one coil (40) of electrically conductive material through which an electrical current flows when the apparatus is in use. This generates a magnetic field in a region through which flows a fluid the flow of which is to be measured and throughout which there is a uniform weak magnetic field such as the Earth's magnetic field. Electrical circuitry (46 to 52) is connected to the said at least one coil (40) to switch on and abruptly switch off such an electrical current. There is an NMR sensor (42) connected to the electrical circuitry (46 to 52) to provide a measure of the decay in the NMR signal from nuclei within such fluid following the abrupt switching off of such an electrical current. A processor (52) of the electrical circuitry (46 to 52) is formed and/or programmed to provide a measure of the flow of such fluid from the said measure of the decay. Also, a method of measuring the flow of a fluid using such a flowmeter.

outputs.L2:
A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) flowmeter includes one or more coils (40) made from an electrically conducting material. During operation, electric current passes through the coil or coils, producing a magnetic field in an area traversed by the fluid whose flow rate is to be determined. That area is also subject to a weak, substantially uniform magnetic field, for example the magnetic field of the Earth.

Electronic circuitry (46 to 52) is coupled to the coil or coils (40) and is arranged to energize the coil current and then terminate it suddenly. An NMR sensor (42), also coupled to the circuitry (46 to 52), supplies an indication of how the NMR signal from nuclei in the fluid diminishes after the current has been rapidly turned off. A processor (52) within the circuitry (46 to 52) is configured, by construction and/or programming, to derive a measurement of the fluid flow from that signal-decay information.

The disclosure also includes a method for determining the flow of a fluid by employing such an NMR flowmeter.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) flowmeter designed to measure the flow rate of a fluid. The flowmeter is configured so that a fluid passes through a defined fluid-flow region where NMR-based measurements can be performed.

The flowmeter includes at least one electrically conductive coil positioned to generate a magnetic field within the fluid-flow region. When an electric current is supplied to the coil, the resulting magnetic field interacts with nuclei in the fluid, preparing them for an NMR measurement.

The system further includes electrical circuitry connected to the coil. This circuitry is arranged to switch the coil current on for a selected period of time and then switch the current off abruptly. The rapid interruption of the current creates suitable conditions for detecting a nuclear magnetic resonance response from the nuclei in the fluid.

After the coil current has been switched off, an NMR sensor detects the resulting NMR signal produced by the nuclei in the fluid. In particular, the sensor measures the decay of the NMR signal over time. This decay contains information related to the movement of the fluid through the measurement region.

A processor is coupled to the NMR sensor and receives data representing the measured NMR signal decay. The processor analyzes the decay characteristics and uses them to determine the flow rate of the fluid. In this way, the flowmeter provides a means of measuring fluid flow based on nuclear magnetic resonance behavior following controlled magnetic-field excitation.
outputs.L4:
A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) flowmeter and associated method are provided for measuring the flow rate of a fluid without requiring the use of a strong externally applied magnetic field. The device operates in the presence of a relatively weak, substantially uniform magnetic field, such as the Earth’s magnetic field or another low-intensity bias field. A coil is positioned around or near a conduit through which the fluid flows. When an electric current is supplied to the coil, the coil generates an additional magnetic field that acts on the nuclear spins of particles within the flowing fluid.

During operation, the current through the coil is maintained for a selected period so that the nuclear spins in the fluid are influenced by the combined magnetic field. The current is then abruptly switched off, causing a rapid change in the magnetic environment experienced by the fluid. This sudden change produces a detectable nuclear magnetic resonance response. The resulting NMR signal decays over time, and the characteristics of this decay are affected by the movement of the fluid through the measurement region.

A detector receives the NMR signal generated after the coil current is interrupted. The detected signal may include information such as signal amplitude, decay rate, phase, frequency, or other time-dependent features associated with the relaxation and transport of the magnetized fluid. A processor analyzes the measured decay signal and determines the fluid flow rate from the observed NMR behavior. In particular, the processor may compare the decay characteristics with calibration data, mathematical models, or previously measured reference values to calculate the velocity or volumetric flow of the fluid.

Because the system relies on the transient NMR response produced by switching off the current-carrying coil in a weak uniform magnetic field, it avoids the need for large permanent magnets or high-field electromagnets typically associated with conventional NMR devices. This allows the flowmeter to be made more compact, less expensive, and easier to install in industrial, laboratory, medical, or field environments. The technique can be applied to a variety of fluids containing nuclei capable of producing an NMR signal, and it provides a non-invasive or minimally invasive way to measure flow through a pipe, tube, channel, or other fluid passage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an NMR flowmeter that uses a coil to generate a magnetic field, abruptly switches the current off, senses NMR signal decay in a weak ambient field such as Earth's magnetic field, and calculates fluid flow from that decay.
counterfactuals.output: An NMR flowmeter includes a flow conduit, a magnetizing coil disposed to apply a magnetic field to fluid within the conduit, a switching circuit configured to abruptly interrupt current through the coil, and a sensing coil or receiver configured to detect nuclear magnetic resonance signals from the fluid after interruption of the current. Following removal of the applied field, nuclear spins precess and decay in a weak ambient magnetic field, such as the Earth’s magnetic field, and the receiver acquires the resulting NMR decay signal. A processor determines one or more decay characteristics, including signal amplitude, phase, frequency, relaxation time, or time-of-flight-related attenuation, and calculates a flow parameter of the fluid based on the detected decay. The flowmeter thereby measures flow without requiring a permanent magnet or high-field NMR magnet, using transient polarization from the coil and detection in the ambient field.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style summary of an apparatus and method for measuring fluid flow using nuclear magnetic resonance, including a conductive coil, switching circuitry, an NMR sensor, and a processor.
counterfactuals.output:
An apparatus for measuring fluid flow includes a conduit configured to receive a flowing fluid, a conductive coil disposed adjacent to or around the conduit, switching circuitry coupled to the conductive coil, a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) sensor arranged to detect NMR response signals from nuclei in the fluid, and a processor coupled to the switching circuitry and the NMR sensor. The switching circuitry is configured to selectively energize the conductive coil to generate a magnetic field and to interrupt or reverse current through the coil to produce a time-varying magnetic field that encodes flow-dependent information in the fluid. The NMR sensor detects resulting resonance signals from the fluid, and the processor analyzes the detected signals to determine a fluid flow parameter, including flow velocity, volumetric flow rate, or flow profile.

A method for measuring fluid flow includes positioning a fluid within a sensing region associated with a conductive coil and an NMR sensor, applying controlled current to the conductive coil via switching circuitry to generate a magnetic-field sequence, exciting or detecting nuclear magnetic resonance in the fluid, acquiring NMR signals representative of motion of the fluid through the sensing region, and processing the acquired signals to compute a measure of fluid flow. The processing may include comparing phase shifts, signal attenuation, time-of-flight characteristics, or resonance changes caused by the imposed magnetic-field sequence to determine the flow parameter.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent application describing a nuclear magnetic resonance flowmeter in which current through a coil is switched on and suddenly off, and the subsequent NMR decay of nuclei in the flowing fluid is used to determine flow rate.
counterfactuals.output: A nuclear magnetic resonance flowmeter for measuring the flow rate of a fluid containing nuclei having magnetic moments includes a coil disposed about a flow passage and means for selectively applying an electric current to the coil to establish a magnetic field in the fluid. The current is maintained for a time sufficient to polarize the nuclei and is then rapidly interrupted, producing a sudden collapse of the magnetic field. Following interruption of the current, the precessing nuclear magnetization generates a time-dependent NMR decay signal in a receiving coil or in the same coil operated in a receiving mode. Signal-processing circuitry detects the amplitude, phase, frequency, or decay envelope of the induced NMR signal and correlates the detected decay with the transit of polarized fluid through the measurement region. The resulting measurement is used to determine the velocity or volumetric flow rate of the fluid. The apparatus provides a nonintrusive flow measurement technique suitable for fluids containing NMR-active nuclei and may compensate for relaxation characteristics, magnetic field strength, and fluid composition.

counterfactuals.output: An NMR-based flowmeter is disclosed for determining a flow characteristic of a fluid. The flowmeter includes a conduit for carrying the fluid, a coil positioned to generate a magnetic field in the fluid when energized by an electrical current, control electronics configured to pulse the current through the coil and thereafter interrupt the current, and a magnetic resonance sensor configured to detect a decay signal from nuclear magnetic resonance of nuclei in the fluid in the presence of the Earth’s magnetic field. Processing circuitry receives the detected decay signal and determines a fluid flow parameter based at least in part on characteristics of the decay signal. The system enables flow measurement using the Earth’s magnetic field as a reference field and transient excitation produced by the current-carrying coil.
